This PR adds a Snakefile and some supporting changes to start building an integration workflow.

I'm not sure it fully addresses https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/sc-data-integration/issues/36, but it is probably most of it?

Note that it is stacked on #62, because I wanted to have some actual integration steps.

I followed the same environment building steps as in https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/scpca-downstream-analyses/pull/166, so the setup instructions are the same:

`snakemake --use-conda -c2 build_renv` to build the environment, unless you are on an M1, in which case you will need
`CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 snakemake --use-conda --conda-create-envs-only -c2 build_renv` the first time. After that, if the `renv.lock` changes, running `snakemake --use-conda -c2 build_renv` should work to update the renv environment.

I could make updating the renv part of the workflow as well by making the renv directory part of the inputs for all scripts, but that seemed like a bit of overkill at this point. If we start to run into problems with out of date environments we could add that, but it might cause rerunning everything if the renv changes, which seems less than ideal much of the time (it isn't crazy either though!).

I used [PEP](http://pep.databio.org/en/latest/simple_example/) to load the project file, which is used to create the full array of samples for integration. I did end up using the latest version of the spec, which means that you have to have the latest version of `snakemake` and `peppy` installed. So in whatever environment you are using to launch snakemake workflows, you may want to run `mamba update snakemake peppy` or `conda update snakemake peppy`

There isn't any really good reason to use PEP in this case, but it does save us from having to load `pandas` on our own, so I thought that was a win.

You'll also note that I changed a number of scripts to suppress package startup messages because `SingleCellExperiment` is very chatty! I didn't quiet everything else (readr messsages for example), but we might want to do that too.


### Questions for reviewers

- This is a good time to think about directory structure! The inputs and outputs defined here are pretty easy to adjust, but we might want to settle on some conventions. In particular, we have a mix of `-` and `_` separation in directories, as well as different levels of nesting for merged `anndata` vs. `sce` files.

- I added the merging step as part of the workflow, with the thought that we would only need to run step 01 (downstream analysis) before everything  can be run by this workflow. Does that make sense to everyone else?
  - As part of this, I moved the conversion of merged sce files to anndata up a directory level, and named it with an `02a` prefix for sorting.

- You might note a funny little thing where the input for the integration is the full directory of merged files. This is because we do all the merging in a single step, so the output of that rule is a directory. So we have to use that for snakemake to be able to backtrack, but then the file name gets created in `params`, which it can use the wildcards it found in the output file. Honestly, I think it is kind of slick, but I wanted to make sure my comment there was sufficient for understanding. 

- At this stage, there is no config file. I didn't see obvious things to put there once the pepfile was used, but if you have ideas of things that should move there, we can certainly make one.

## About The Pull Request

Removes from the nuclear operative uplink:
Riot Darts and Toy Guns (from Nuclear Ops, not Clown Ops)
Camera Bug
Combat Gloves Plus (they were removed from the leader already)
FRAME disc
Guerrilla Gloves
Radioactive Microlaser
Blood-Red Magboots (the standalone ones)
Power Beacon
Bioterror everything (including the bundle)
Stechkin APS machine pistol
AI Detector

## Why It's Good For The Game

These items are either really bad, entirely useless, done better by other items or truly just broken.

We know there are a lot of bundles with a few of these items still in. We're not dealing with the bundles entirely just yet. Bioterror bundle just happened to have quite literally only items I was already removing, so I feel pretty confident getting rid of it here.

<details>
<summary>Overwritten explanations inside</summary>

**Donksoft weaponry:** It's really weird that nukies can get these. They're meant to be the lethal variety of the two operative groups we have, and I think Pacifist is no longer able to be kept as an operative. Let's keep the toy guns to the clowns. Just kill people.

**Camera Bug:** Actually pretty nonfunctional right now, and generally not especially useful to ops, who possess an advanced camera aboard their ship. They also cannot really go around bugging cameras very easily, nor do they get very much use from it. They simply have better tools and options.

**FRAME Disc:** A method of acquiring a normal traitor uplink as a nuclear operative. This doesn't do much good for them, as most of the truly spicy items are at least 30 minutes deep and they can't use the FRAME uplink to do objectives. Still, better to resolve this oversight while we're here, they certainly can't do much with this item.

**Radioactive Microlaser:** Just use CQC.

**Power Beacon:** I question why this is even available to anyone who isn't a station engineer or atmospheric technician traitor. But ops definitely have even less business causing a singularity unless they're using a saboteur borg, and even then, they're potentially screwing themselves over massively by doing so as a singularity is entirely indiscriminate. Better to just not let newer players confuse this for the actually useful item, the power sink.

**The Bioterror Line:** These are extremely outdated items, using fairly neutered chems by this point. The dart pistol and chemical sprayer in a previous PR are both bundled with their respective labs, so operatives wanting to make use of chemical mischief can now just kinda do that without much unnecessary expense. Additionally, while they can still totally make good use of chemical kits thanks to this, they don't get a whole lot out of the bioterror prepackaged items to begin with. Their mixes are kind of dreadful, since they're usually fairly small dosages, so they get processed out of the body almost immediately. In the case of the bioterror grenades, someone thought mute toxin, itching powder and spore toxin in a foam reaction would do something worth a damn for ops. Ops can make their own grenade mixes, so we can just let them make their own killer concoctions using the available kit and the chem dispenser.

**AI Detector:** Ops have quite a lot of anti-AI tech right from the moment they spawn. No suit sensors, agent cards prevent tracking, and ops can just blow up AIs using explosives if they really want. Ops can also send in borgs to execute the AI. They usually move pretty damn fast through the station, so most AIs can't easily lock down the entire force, nor can they keep them locked down. They don't get much out of knowing an AI is watching them. Additionally, this items been pretty significantly reworked to the point that I think it has fairly dubious value inherently, but even before that, this wasn't a particularly useful item.

**Stechkin APS machine pistol:** I kind of wish this had a place, but we have so many automatic weapons for ops already and this one is the most superfluous. I brought it into the world, I'm taking it out. There just isn't any noticable benefits to this over the c20-r. Pyro bundle still comes with the APS if you want it.

**Guerrilla Gloves:** Fikou already got rid of the Krav gloves from Nukies with the promise we'd look at maybe reintroducing them or rethinking their presence in the arsenal, as gloves are overridden by modsuits. The same can also be said of tackler gloves to some degree, but neither of us are making promises of a return. I think as a standard, op equipment should be a little more reliable than a pure RNG stun, and they certainly have plenty of that already. 
</details>

author: dstufft
body:
This goes back to some of the very earliest code in Warehouse.

So currently Warehouse allows us to mark a route such that it is "read only", which has the effect of using the ``SERIALIABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE`` transaction isolation level on those views, currently only in use on the JSON and Simple API.

The history here is that originally Warehouse just used ``READ COMITTED`` for everything, however that caused a bug in Bandersnatch where it would "miss" some updates made to the Simple API. This was discussed in length in https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/issues/405 but the tl;dr was that our query pattern looked like:

1. Query for the Project + Release
2. Query for the Serial
3. Query for the Files

Which meant that we were running into cases where we would get a serial that didn't match the data that we were sending to Bandersnatch. 

This was particularly problematic because (1) was being run by Pyramid under the covers and (2) was happening in our views, so what would happen a transaction could get committed between 1 and 2, and Bandersnatch would think that it had the most up to date data, but in reality, the data selected in (1) was stale.

We fixed this by switching all of PyPI to use ``SERIALIZABLE``, but that was causing **HEAVY** lock contention, so we ended up backing that off and using ``READ COMMITTED`` for most of the site and using ``SERIALIZABLE`` just for the views where strong consistency mattered. Even that was getting heavy lock contention, which lead us to where we are today where we switched those views to use ``SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE`` which takes a big up-front lock, but then removes that transaction from locking completely after that.

This PR simplifies this and moves the entire site over to using ``READ COMMITTED``, it does this because in the interim years we've adjusted things and now (1) includes the serial number, so our very first query select the serial number, which means we eliminate the problem of stale data being included with an up-to-date serial number.

This PR does enable one more possible scenario, which is that new data can be served to bandersnatch using an older serial. This is actually fine, because bandersnatch will keep retrying until it gets the newer serial number, so while it may mean it thinks it's not up to date while it is, it doesn't cause it to miss any data.

This should help reduce overall lock contention in PyPI, and make it simpler to scale out these read only endpoints.

body:
This PR updates [attrs](https://pypi.org/project/attrs) from **21.2.0** to **22.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 22.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

Backwards-incompatible Changes
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Python 2.7 is not supported anymore.

  Dealing with Python 2.7 tooling has become too difficult for a volunteer-run project.

  We have supported Python 2 more than 2 years after it was officially discontinued and feel that we have paid our dues.
  All version up to 21.4.0 from December 2021 remain fully functional, of course.
  `936 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/936>`_
- The deprecated ``cmp`` attribute of ``attrs.Attribute`` has been removed.
  This does not affect the *cmp* argument to ``attr.s`` that can be used as a shortcut to set *eq* and *order* at the same time.
  `939 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/939>`_


Changes
^^^^^^^

- Instantiation of frozen slotted classes is now faster.
  `898 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/898>`_
- If an ``eq`` key is defined, it is also used before hashing the attribute.
  `909 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/909>`_
- Added ``attrs.validators.min_len()``.
  `916 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/916>`_
- ``attrs.validators.deep_iterable()``'s *member_validator* argument now also accepts a list of validators and wraps them in an ``attrs.validators.and_()``.
  `925 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/925>`_
- Added missing type stub re-imports for ``attrs.converters`` and ``attrs.filters``.
  `931 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/931>`_
- Added missing stub for ``attr(s).cmp_using()``.
  `949 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/949>`_
- ``attrs.validators._in()``'s ``ValueError`` is not missing the attribute, expected options, and the value it got anymore.
  `951 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/951>`_
- Python 3.11 is now officially supported.
  `969 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/969>`_


----
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.4.0
   ```
   -------------------

Changes
^^^^^^^

- Fixed the test suite on PyPy3.8 where ``cloudpickle`` does not work.
  `892 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/892>`_
- Fixed ``coverage report`` for projects that use ``attrs`` and don't set a ``--source``.
  `895 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/895>`_,
  `896 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/896>`_


----
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

Backward-incompatible Changes
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- When using ``define``, converters are now run by default when setting an attribute on an instance -- additionally to validators.
  I.e. the new default is ``on_setattr=[attrs.setters.convert, attrs.setters.validate]``.

  This is unfortunately a breaking change, but it was an oversight, impossible to raise a ``DeprecationWarning`` about, and it's better to fix it now while the APIs are very fresh with few users.
  `835 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/835>`_,
  `886 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/886>`_
- ``import attrs`` has finally landed!
  As of this release, you can finally import ``attrs`` using its proper name.

  Not all names from the ``attr`` namespace have been transferred; most notably ``attr.s`` and ``attr.ib`` are missing.
  See ``attrs.define`` and ``attrs.field`` if you haven't seen our next-generation APIs yet.
  A more elaborate explanation can be found `On The Core API Names <https://www.attrs.org/en/latest/names.html>`_

  This feature is at least for one release **provisional**.
  We don't *plan* on changing anything, but such a big change is unlikely to go perfectly on the first strike.

  The API docs have been mostly updated, but it will be an ongoing effort to change everything to the new APIs.
  Please note that we have **not** moved -- or even removed -- anything from ``attr``!

  Please do report any bugs or documentation inconsistencies!
  `887 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/887>`_


Changes
^^^^^^^

- ``attr.asdict(retain_collection_types=False)`` (default) dumps collection-esque keys as tuples.
  `646 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/646>`_,
  `888 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/888>`_
- ``__match_args__`` are now generated to support Python 3.10's
  `Structural Pattern Matching <https://docs.python.org/3.10/whatsnew/3.10.html#pep-634-structural-pattern-matching>`_.
  This can be controlled by the ``match_args`` argument to the class decorators on Python 3.10 and later.
  On older versions, it is never added and the argument is ignored.
  `815 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/815>`_
- If the class-level *on_setattr* is set to ``attrs.setters.validate`` (default in ``define`` and ``mutable``) but no field defines a validator, pretend that it's not set.
  `817 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/817>`_
- The generated ``__repr__`` is significantly faster on Pythons with f-strings.
  `819 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/819>`_
- Attributes transformed via ``field_transformer`` are wrapped with ``AttrsClass`` again.
  `824 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/824>`_
- Generated source code is now cached more efficiently for identical classes.
  `828 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/828>`_
- Added ``attrs.converters.to_bool()``.
  `830 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/830>`_
- ``attrs.resolve_types()`` now resolves types of subclasses after the parents are resolved.
  `842 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/842>`_
  `843 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/843>`_
- Added new validators: ``lt(val)`` (< val), ``le(va)`` (≤ val), ``ge(val)`` (≥ val), ``gt(val)`` (> val), and ``maxlen(n)``.
  `845 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/845>`_
- ``attrs`` classes are now fully compatible with `cloudpickle <https://github.com/cloudpipe/cloudpickle>`_ (no need to disable ``repr`` anymore).
  `857 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/857>`_
- Added new context manager ``attrs.validators.disabled()`` and functions ``attrs.validators.(set|get)_disabled()``.
  They deprecate ``attrs.(set|get)_run_validators()``.
  All functions are interoperable and modify the same internal state.
  They are not – and never were – thread-safe, though.
  `859 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/859>`_
- ``attrs.validators.matches_re()`` now accepts pre-compiled regular expressions in addition to pattern strings.
  `877 <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/877>`_

body:
Removes usage of std::set in ResidencySet and replaces it with a std::vector.
This does allow duplicate heaps to be inserted into the ResidencySet,
however insertion will be O(1) instead of O(log(n)) and instead we can
easily identify duplicate heaps by checking their last used fence value
when during iteration.

## 🗒️ What

Applies the docs route setup techniques used when onboarding Terraform in #749 to all other products.

## 🤷 Why

- Reduces boilerplate required to set up docs routes
- Standardizes on `rootDocsPaths` config in `src/data` product.json files
- Consistency, all `<productSlug>/<docsCategory>` page files now function in the same way
- Preparing for a potential future abstraction where docs routes do not have separate page files

- Uses existing `getRootDocsPathGenerationFunctions` introduced in #749 
- Adds `getAdditionalRemarkPlugins` & `generateGetScope` functions to handle per-product exceptions, such as for Sentinel and Vagrant, without requiring config in `page` files
- Adds pass-through support for `mainBranch` & `basePathForLoader` options for remote docs loading, which are necessary for some products, such as Packer and Sentinel

author: yinweisu
body:
*Issue #, if available:*

*Description of changes:*
* Added ImageCloudPredictor. API and usage are as follow:
  * Training: user needs to pass an argument `image_path`, which is a local path or s3 path to the images, to `fit()`.
  * General workflow is to archive the images, upload to s3 and setup the channel to sagemaker. Within the container, we uncompress the archive and do fit.
```python
"""
image_path: str, default = None
  A local path or s3 path to the images. If you provided this parameter, the image path inside your train/tune data MUST be relative.
  If local path, path needs to be either a compressed file containing the images or a folder containing the images.
  If it's a folder, we will zip it for you and upload it to the s3.
  If s3 path, the path needs to be a path to a compressed file containing the images
"""
```
  * Realtime inference:
  * General workflow is to detect images from dataframe and converting them into numpy arrays. Pass numpy arrays as payload to the endpoint. In the endpoint, we decrypt the array, save them as files, and pass file paths to predictor.
```python
def predict_real_time(self, test_data, test_data_image_column=None, accept='application/x-parquet'):
        """
        Predict with the deployed SageMaker endpoint. A deployed SageMaker endpoint is required.
        This is intended to provide a low latency inference.
        If you want to inference on a large dataset, use `predict()` instead.

        Parameters
        ----------
        test_data: Union(str, pandas.DataFrame)
            The test data to be inferenced.
            Can be a pandas.DataFrame, a numpy.ndarray, a local path or a s3 path to a csv file containing paths of test images.
            Or a local path to a single image file.
            Or a list of local paths to image files.
        test_data_image_column: Optional(str)
            If provided a pandas.DataFrame as the test_data, you must specify the column name corresponding to image paths
            Images has to live in the same directory specified by the column.
        accept: str, default = application/x-parquet
            Type of accept output content.
            Valid options are application/x-parquet, text/csv, application/json
        """
```
  * Batch inference: user needs to pass `test_data` as a path to a directory containing the images to `predict()`
  * Upload image folders directly to s3, and use transformers with `content_type = 'application/x-image'`, which is natively supported by batch transform.
```python
"""
test_data: str
  The test data to be inferenced. Can be a local path or a s3 path to a directory containing the images.
"""
```
* Added unit tests for ImageCloudPredictor
* Updated the way to detect large payload size when doing realtime inference. Previously, we calculate the payload size ourselves. However, that calculation was inaccurate. Now, we catch the error and warn user instead.

body:
…or page

Signed-off-by: David Kwon <dakwon@redhat.com>

<!-- Please review the following before submitting a PR:
Che's Contributing Guide: https://github.com/eclipse/che/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
Pull Request Policy: https://github.com/eclipse/che/wiki/Development-Workflow#pull-requests

COMMITTERS: please include labels on each PR. Labels are listed here: https://github.com/eclipse/che/wiki/Labels but at a minimum you should include `kind/..` and `Dev Open Pull Request Status` labels.
-->

### What does this PR do?

Currently there is a generic error page that is displayed when trying to access a workspace url (a devworkspace's `status.mainUrl`) when the workspace is not running:

However, there can be multiple reasons why a workspace is not running. Some examples are:
 - workspace is not running because it was shut down due to inactivity
 - workspace is not running because it was shut down due to the run timeout
 - workspace shut down because an error (ie case where for the devworkspace, `status.phase == Failed`)
 - user forgot to start the workspace
 
This PR introduces a new class [WorkspaceStoppedDetector](https://github.com/eclipse-che/che-dashboard/blob/f012219156b24a8c6ba091bd5ae81b2c008d73eb/packages/dashboard-frontend/src/services/bootstrap/workspaceStoppedDetector.ts) to help detect the different cases.
 
Ad a result, different error page messages in each of these four scenarios are available:

<details>
<summary>Workspace inactivity</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83611742/181825169-0b3ea2b6-5d66-40e2-9d48-3c2da6bc8c63.png)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Workspace run timeout</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83611742/181825430-85e82568-81e8-4e31-b02a-e7f1d5a6fa26.png)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Workspace error</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83611742/181825565-bf664356-ea60-45b2-9d9d-633010d2dfcf.png)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Workspace was not started</summary>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83611742/181825481-5049a5c0-060a-43f7-8721-5930a68a0e67.png)

</details>



### What issues does this PR fix or reference?
Fixes https://github.com/eclipse/che/issues/21516


### Is it tested? How?
<!-- 
Please provide instructions here which scenario you fix/implement
and in which way you tested it, provide as much as you think reviewer
needs to do the same.
-->



#### Testing the 'Workspace inactivity' error page
1. Set the workspace inactivity timeout to a smaller value by setting `checluster.spec.devEnvironments.secondsOfInactivityBeforeIdling` to, for example, `120`.

2. Start a workspace. Once the editor opens, let it timeout by not interacting with it for about 120 seconds.

3. Once the workspace times out, refresh the page


#### Testing the 'Workspace run timeout' error page
1. Set the workspace run timeout to a value smaller than the inactivity timeout by setting `checluster.spec.devEnvironments.secondsOfRunBeforeIdling` to, for example, `80`.

2. Start a workspace. After the workspace starts, the workspace should terminate in about 80 seconds.

3. Once the workspace times out, refresh the editor page

#### Testing the 'Workspace error' error page
1. To prevent other timeouts from shutting down the workspace, disable the timeouts by setting both `secondsOfInactivityBeforeIdling` and `secondsOfRunBeforeIdling` to `-1` in the `checluster` CR.

2. Start a workspace with this github repository: https://github.com/dkwon17/failing-workspace/tree/fail-delayed

3. The editor should open, however after roughly 1 minute and 30 seconds, the workspace should terminate due to a failing container.

4. Refresh the editor page

#### Testing the 'Workspace was not started' error page
1. Start a workspace.

2. Once the workspace has started and the editor has loaded, stop the workspace.

3. Refresh the editor page

#### Release Notes
<!-- markdown to be included in marketing announcement - N/A for bugs -->
The warning page that appears when accessing the workspace url for a stopped workspace provides a more specific message depending on the reason why the workspace has stopped.

The cases are:
* Workspace has been stopped due to inactivity
* Workspace has been stopped because it reached the run timeout
* Workspace has stopped due to an error causing the workspace pod to shut down
* Workspace was not running in the first place

Both will be merged at the same time. -->

author: terrelln
body:
Fixes #3211.

Adds the `--[no-]pass-through` flag which enables/disables pass-through mode.

* `zstdcat`, `zcat`, and `gzcat` default to `--pass-through`.
  Pass-through mode can be disabled by passing `--no-pass-through`.
* All other binaries default to not setting pass-through mode.
  However, we preserve the legacy behavior of enabling pass-through
  mode when writing to stdout with `-f` set, unless pass-through
  mode is explicitly disabled with `--no-pass-through`.

Adds a new test for this behavior that should codify the behavior we want.

body:
## Describe your changes and why you are making these changes
Main purpose was to address https://linear.app/aqueducthq/issue/ENG-1403/remove-warnings-about-overriding-an-existing-operator. I also took the chance to clean up our logging a little bit:
- `Logger.logger.info(...)` seemed pretty redundant. I don't see why we can't use `logger().info(..)`. We're not supposed to call functions from the root logger like `logging.info(..)`.
- Instead of adding a verbose flag, we can have the user configure the client with the correct logging level, the same way Ray does it https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/package-ref.html#ray-remote. 

I'm also fine with us exposing a `verbose` argument and mapping that to `log.INFO`, whereas it's regularly `log.WARNING`. What do you think? I'd like to also be able to set log level to be DEBUG whenever I want, and I wasn't sure if that level should be included in verbose mode.

This means that first, players do not need to be removed at the end of the list, for example :bring all,-%TEAM can now be written as :bring -%TEAM,all and function the same way.

Second Change:
Additionally, the random and #NUMBER sections have been moved to the end, which ensures both that the random player will not be one already selected, and also will not be one purposely removed with the -Name. This means that a command such as :bring random,-%TEAM,-%TEAM2 will bring a player who is not on TEAM1 or TEAM2, where previously, if the random player was on one of these teams, the command would just bring no players.

Third Change:
Because this reformating may result in some unintentional issues, such as :bring all,-%TEAM,scel, where scel is a player on the team not adding scel to those being brought, there is now a +Name section, so in order to achieve the desired effect, the admin would just have to run :bring all,-%TEAM,+scel. 

Final Change:
the !usage command has been edited to reflect these changes.

author: bpkroth
body:
This change set handles publishing docker containers to an upstream docker registry (currently ACR) after successful builds for approved PRs merged to `main`.  To account for security fixes in the container images, a nightly build job was also added.

The PR also splits the published containers into `benchbase-dev` with a JDK for the devcontainer and `benchbase` with a JRE for the runtime only version (previously both contained a full JDK).  The later contains all profiles.  Alternatively, there are singleton profile images (e.g. `benchbase-postgres`).  This, along with some internal file deduplication, improves container size.
Additionally, some tweaks were made to allow building each profile in parallel within the devcontainer.

While doing that a race in test target execution was noticed when multiple maven threads are allowed to run.
For now, we have simply disabled parallelism for the test target.

Currently, the images are published as `latest` however, can also be generated for tagged `v2022` style releases.

Some documentation and CI tests are also included.

author: mgartner
body:
The `SimplifySelectFilters` normalization rule now transforms filters to
`false` if any of the filter items are contradictions. This allows
filters to be simplified in more cases, which can trigger other rules.
This can eliminate non-leakproof expressions in filters and allow
`SimplifyZeroCardinalityGroup` to fire.

For example, consider the query:

    SELECT a, b FROM t WHERE a > 0 AND a < 0 AND 1/b = 1

Prior to this commit, it could not be simplified to an empty values
clause because the non-leakproof division operator prevents
SimplifyZeroCardinalityGroup from applying. The normalized plan would
be:

    select
     ├── columns: a:1 b:2
     ├── cardinality: [0 - 0]
     ├── immutable
     ├── scan t
     │    └── columns: a:1 b:2
     └── filters
          ├── (a:1 > 0) AND (a:1 < 0) [constraints=(contradiction)]
          └── (1 / b:2) = 1 [outer=(2), immutable]

Now, `SimplifySelectFilters` eliminates the division operator, making
the expression leakproof, and allowing `SimplifyZeroCardinalityGroup` to
apply. The normalized plan is now:

    values
     ├── columns: a:1!null b:2!null
     ├── cardinality: [0 - 0]
     ├── key: ()
     └── fd: ()-->(1-2)

Release note (performance improvement): The optimizer can detect
contradictory filters in more cases, leading to more efficient query
plans.

author: conrad-t-pino
body:
For many years a client accumulated many image files and most are for email messages. The primary motivation for this change is direct access to image binary for inclusion in email message without any intermediate file operations and later HTTP requests.

Change summary:
- Translate CFML tags in components and templates into CFScript for brevity - we're Java hacks :smiley_cat:
- Refactor `Barcode.cfc` and `QRCode.cfc` common methods into `abstract` `ZXing.cfc` component
- Add `ZXing.cfc` `readBinary` method for use from `Barcode.cfc` and `QRCode.cfc` components
- `index.cfm` and `barcode.cfm` HTML 5 markup
- ZXing version 2.1 to 3.5.0 upgrade
- `README.md` updates

ZXing `Codabar` change status:
- ZXing `Codabar` implmentation changed breaking the third `barcode.cfm` example
- ZXing v2.1 accepts `A` and `N` as start and end characters where `A` is "standard" and `N` is "alternate"
- ZXing v3.5.0 expects start and end characters from the same set, rejecting mixed set combinations
- Replacing `N` end character with `A` resolves the third `barcode.cfm` example

Testing status:
- `index.cfm` and `barcode.cfm` both create their respective images

This submission is a draft for project review while we continue testing and deployment from this branch.

author: grondo
body:
Problem: When recursive top_create() fails due to a `flux_open()` error, e.g. the user cannot access the job's URI, top exits with an error when the intention is just to fall back to the current top instance.

This PR removes some calls to `fatal()` in `top_create()` and instead passes errors back via a `flux_error_t`. On error, a popup dialog is displayed instead of raising a fatal error. The dialog is dismissed after 4s or if any key is pressed.

This PR makes use of `flux_open_ex(3)`, so is based on top of #4450. In addition, the internal `uri_resolve()` function is augmented similarly to `flux_open_ex(3)` so that errors to `stderr` from `popen2()` of `flux uri` are captured.

Example of error popup:

![Screenshot from 2022-07-29 11-10-17](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/741970/181849076-4298af1e-0ef7-43a5-a1a8-610d59af21cf.png)

author: dmaillouxpanw
body:
## Description

TG was updated due to an out of date dependency on [golang.org/x/sys/unix](http://golang.org/x/sys/unix). This PR integrates this update so it can be exposed to users of mtlsproxy. I am ok if someone wants to submit a better PR with more sanity checks and testing or provide detailed feedback so I can do so.

## Motivation and Context

Some Mac users were experiencing issues with the old [golang.org/x/sys/unix](http://golang.org/x/sys/unix) dependency. It was failing as follows:
```
workspace/code/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/sys@v0.0.0-20190626221950-04f50cda93cb/unix/zsyscall_darwin_arm64.go:28:3: //go:linkname must refer to declared function or variable
```

## How Has This Been Tested?

I tested this by installing in Apomux install/install using the branch name. However this may require further testing to ensure nothing else is broken as a result of the change. I have not run any other tests so I am unsure if this will still behave normally otherwise.

## Types of changes

- (Possibly, not sure) Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
There does not appear to be any local tests present to determine if dependency changes have broken any feature. Not sure if there are external tests that can be run to determine this.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [ ] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** document.
- [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes if appropriate.
- [ ] All new and existing tests passed.
